content.text:
This confirms it: the pre-existing early-return `!arena.inArena((Player) event.getEntity())` guard was dropped during the refactor, so any player (even those not in the arena) would have their food-level events cancelled while the arena was running — exactly the bug the fix commit addresses by re-adding `arena.inArena(p) &&`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: a9c1ded76ed1fc157add8ef73565bd6112967bf1

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the history of `ArenaListener.java`'s `onFoodLevelChange` method with `git log -p --follow`, searching for prior occurrences of the `lockFoodLevel` condition that the fix commit touches, to find where the surrounding logic was last restructured.

(2) Commit `a9c1ded7` refactored `onFoodLevelChange` from:
```java
if (!arena.isRunning()) return;
if (!(event.getEntity() instanceof Player) || !arena.inArena((Player) event.getEntity())) return;
if (lockFoodLevel) event.setCancelled(true);
```
into a two-branch structure (`isRunning()` vs. lobby/spec), but in doing so it dropped the `arena.inArena(p)` check entirely — the new "running" branch cancels food-level changes for *any* player as long as `lockFoodLevel` is true, regardless of whether that player is actually inside the arena.

(3) The fix commit (`5058c479`) simply reinstates that missing guard by changing `if (lockFoodLevel)` back to `if (arena.inArena(p) && lockFoodLevel)`, restoring the exact check that was lost in `a9c1ded7`. This is a direct, minimal correction of the omission, giving high confidence this is the introducing commit.

I'm confident in this identification — the diffs align precisely (removed check → later re-added identical check), and no other commit touches this condition in between.
